The judgments I made

You asked me to decide; here is each call and why. All of them are reversible in Swap pieces.

  1. Topper: Tied from 6" natural jute (B0DQ4BXYKZ): a 78" strip and an 8" knot piece, two 10" loops angled up about 20 degrees over two 14" tails, as on the board (the earlier 22" tails were 60% too long). 24 black felt paws of 3", about half the ribbon's width like the board's, on the front face only; floral wire glued along both back edges holds the unwired jute. Full cut list, knot, fray stop, tracing (white fabric marker) and fixing steps are on its page.
  2. Pets: Kept the 12" Cuddlekins golden retriever (a paler gold than the board's). The cats are now the Aurora Miyoni grey tabby (9" long, 6" tall): the board's striped grey-brown coat with a white chest, from a seller with 2,170 ratings. The earlier FLUFFYFUN pick was mostly white and standing, not the sitting tabby the plan claimed. No sitting striped grey tabby of 8-12" reaches Edmonton by Nov 30, so the cats are rated close: ours crouch where the board's sit. The same tabby sits with the dog under the tree.
  3. Doghouses: Six 10" foam-board doghouses at the board's scale, now with every board detail as a cut part: the flat U arch trim, barge boards, threshold, ridge cap and a raised paw (from the door offcut). Bricks score 0.9" x 1.5" through the template with an empty ballpoint, the joints stay dark (dark-brick base, barn red dabbed on the faces), roof undersides are sealed so they do not warp, and each 160 g house is wired upright through its floor. The printed cut plan fits all of it on 9 boards, so 10 still leaves a spare.
  4. Paw ornaments: Ten 6" ornaments: a hoop with only the outer ring primed and gilded (its brass screw reads as the cap), tea-stained Aida for the board's warm biscuit-cream face (9 x 9" pieces so it can be drawn drum-tight), a black glitter-card paw, a black felt back so it is finished from behind, and a bow hand-tied from the dark red velvet. The Faylapa 16-pk hoops are now the default: the same ornament, $37.69 less incl. GST than eleven DeSerres hoops, here Nov 20, with 6 spares; that saving pays for the wire cutter, cutting surface, third clay bag and the bigger Aida.
  5. Bones: Eight 9" bones at the board's chunky biscuit proportions (shaft 0.27, knob span 0.53 of the length, about 1" thick). Clay is calculated from the template outline (31 sq in) less the foil core: about 117 g each, so a third 500 g bag is bought (1,163 g needed for bones and biscuits). Each hangs level like the board from a gold cord whose two ends are glued into holes drilled over wire anchors in the upper knobs.
  6. Baubles: Big balls at the board's 4-6" scale: plain 6" reds (Benjia), 4" red glitter, 4" JOYIN reds and golds, the green glitter and champagne sets, and one 100-pc set to fill. The old 100-pc link now opened a Black & Gold set, so it points to the same seller's Red & Gold set; the 12 green glitter balls give the board's few greens. Patterned and sequin balls hang deep, smooth ones on the tips.
  7. Gifts: Cream burlap ribbon and bows on the gifts, as on the board (1.5" x 20 yd, $18.39), instead of velvet. Tartan paper on three boxes, kraft paw paper on the fourth.
  8. Velvet: The board mixes solid deep red velvet bows with the tartan ones on the tree, so five 9" velvet bows are tied from the spare 1.5" velvet (no extra cost) besides the paw-ornament and jar bows.
  9. Floor and basket: The bowl is now a deep red Bella dog bowl with a steel interior and paw prints, like the board (no paint marker needed). The basket bone toy is a cream sherpa bone with a felt paw (the old link was the grey variant). The lace liner comes out of the basket, the biscuits use the 2.7" cutter, and the throw is draped paw-side out.
  10. Vendors and delivery: Prices re-checked on Nov 16. Delivery is counted per unit on international listings (worst case: the tartan's $5.45 on each of 5 rolls). DeSerres: every default line ships in 48 hours, as one shipment expected Nov 25-27; the committee plan's craft sessions start the clay bones, scarves and paws on Nov 20 with Amazon materials, so only painting waits for DeSerres, and Michaels Edmonton is the fallback if it has not shipped by Nov 19.
  11. Giant doghouse, streamers, gold crown: Off by default: none of them are on the board. Each stays one tap away in Swap pieces.

How we make it: materials, tools and steps

Burlap paw-print bow topper, 22" (DIY) · makes 1

Materials: Natural jute burlap ribbon 6" x 12 yd, hemmed: 2.4 yd; Black felt 8 x 12", 7 sheets: 3.4 sheets; Permanent fabric glue 118 ml (felt and glitter paws, scarf edges): 13.5 ml; Green floral wire 22 gauge, 3 x 118 yd: 5.9 yd; Glue sticks 7 mm, 96 pc: 6 sticks.

Tools: Wire cutter (every floral-wire cut: about 400); Mini hot glue gun (7 mm sticks); Erasable fabric marker, white (traces paws and circles on black felt); Steel and cork ruler 24"; Extra-large moving box 24 x 20 x 20", flattened (the cutting surface under every knife cut); Plastic drop sheet 8 x 12 ft (painting in the office); Scissors (office); Zip ties (2, supplied with the tree).

Cut list from the 6" jute (12 yd roll): one 78" bow strip and one 8" knot piece (2.4 yd with the notches). Work on the drop sheet.

  1. Edge wire: on the back face, hot-glue a 79" length of floral wire 1/4" in from each long edge, folding the last 1/2" of wire back at each end so it cannot poke out. The jute is not wired, so this is what holds the loops.
  2. Paws, front face only: trace 24 paws on the black felt with the 3" template (page 3) and the white fabric marker (or tape the paper paw to the felt and cut round it). Each paw is 5 pieces: a pad and four toes. Glue 23 on the front face of the strip with fabric glue, alternating left and right of the centre line about every 3.4", none in the middle 4" where the bow is pinched; glue the 24th in the middle of the knot piece. Dry flat overnight.
  3. Fray stop: the long edges are hemmed; run a thin bead of fabric glue across the cut ends of the strip and the knot piece.
  4. Tie, paws facing you: leave a 14" tail, make a 10" loop to the left (about 22" of ribbon) and a 10" loop to the right, angling both loops up about 20 degrees, and pinch the centre with an 18" piece of floral wire; the second 14" tail hangs down. Fold the knot piece lengthwise in half (3" wide, paw out), wrap it round the pinch and hot-glue it at the back. V-notch both tails 1" deep and seal the notch with fabric glue.
  5. Fix: zip-tie it to the top stem with two of the organizers' zip ties and twist the 18" wire ends round the stem (two more 18" wires if it leans). Shape the loops up and round and let the tails hang about 25 degrees off vertical, like the board: about 22" across with 14" tails.

Golden retriever plush, sitting 12" · bought, then finished by us

Materials: Green floral wire 22 gauge, 3 x 118 yd: 7 yd.

Tools: Wire cutter (every floral-wire cut: about 400); Zip ties (supplied with the tree).

Red doghouse with brick walls, a cream wood-shingle roof with deep overhang and a ridge cap, an arched door with a thick cream trim and a dark opening, and a cream paw on the gable.

Our verdict: Every board detail is now a cut part on the template (page 8): the flat U arch trim on a cream threshold, barge boards along the front roof edges, a ridge cap and a raised 5-piece paw cut from the door offcut. How we make it: materials, tools and steps

Doghouse ornaments, 10" (DIY) · makes 6

Materials: Green floral wire 22 gauge, 3 x 118 yd: 3.3 yd; Glue sticks 7 mm, 96 pc: 24 sticks; Foam board, white 3/16", 16 x 20": 2880 sq in; Student acrylic Burnt Sienna 250 ml (ships in 48 h): 150.6 ml; White gesso 948 ml (primer; the white in the cream, biscuit and tan mixes): 139.4 ml; Americana acrylic Deep Ochre 59 ml (tints gesso to cream, biscuit and tan): 5.8 ml; Student acrylic Crimson 250 ml (1:1 with Naphthol Red = barn red): 161.8 ml; Americana acrylic Lamp Black 60 ml: 12.4 ml; Student acrylic Naphthol Red 250 ml: 64.5 ml; Metallic yarn, gold, 25 m (hanging loops): 3.6 m.

Tools: Art knife with 5 blades (foam board and cardboard); Steel and cork ruler 24"; Extra-large moving box 24 x 20 x 20", flattened (the cutting surface under every knife cut); Mini hot glue gun (7 mm sticks); Craft brush set, 25 pc (doors, trim, details); Foam brush 1"; Foam brush 2"; Hydra synthetic sponge (brick dabbing, stencilling); Round wood sticks 6 mm x 15 cm, 30 pc (1/4" clay thickness guides, paint stirrers); Wire cutter (every floral-wire cut: about 400); Plastic drop sheet 8 x 12 ft (painting in the office); Pencil and an empty ballpoint pen (office); Toothpicks (6) (office).

Print pages 1, 2 and 8 at Actual size (check the 1" square). Cut on the flattened moving box with a fresh blade against the steel ruler; mark in pencil, never pen. Test the glue gun on an offcut first and glue onto the paper faces, not the bare foam edge (the hot gun melts the foam core).

  1. Cut, per house, following the page-2 cut plan (boards 1-9 hold all six houses; board 10 is spare; measure each board first and if it is under 16" trim the difference off the roof overhang): front with the arched door (keep the door piece), back, two sides, two roofs, floor (page 2), four corner trims (page 2), and from page 8 the flat U-shaped arch trim (cut as one piece), two barge boards (flip one), the threshold and two ridge caps. Cut the 2.5" gable paw (pad + 4 toes, page 8) from the door piece.
  2. Score while the template is still taped on: press the grey brick lines (page 1: courses about 0.9", bricks 1.5", staggered) and the roof board lines (page 2: every 1.25" parallel to the eave, joints every 1.5") through the paper with the empty ballpoint. Score the two plank lines on the threshold.
  3. Paint flat, before assembly: the inside faces of the walls and the undersides of both roofs burnt sienna (stops the foam board warping; dark through the door); the roof tops, trims, threshold and paw one coat of cream (cream = 1/2 cup (120 ml) gesso + 1 tsp deep ochre + a pea-sized dab of burnt sienna; mix one batch for all six houses in a lidded cup and stir with a wood stick).
  4. Assemble with hot glue: the walls round the floor (the floor sits inside the walls), then a toothpick across the inside of the two gable peaks with a 60 cm gold cord tied round it, the doubled loop coming out at the ridge, then the two roofs (3/4" overhang all round) either side of the cord. Poke two holes through the floor 2" apart with a toothpick.
  5. Walls: brush the outside dark brick (dark brick = Crimson + Lamp Black about 10:1) and let it dry, then sponge-dab barn red = Naphthol Red + Crimson 1:1 over the brick faces only, twice, so the scored joints stay dark like the board's.
  6. Second cream coat on the roof, trims, threshold and paw; dry-brush a little sienna along the roof boards for grain. Paint the ridge caps barn red with a touch of sienna.
  7. Trims: glue the four corner trims on the wall corners, the threshold flat at the foot of the door (back edge against the wall, top level with the floor, sticking out 3/4"), the U arch trim round the door with its legs standing on the threshold, the barge boards along the two front roof edges meeting at the peak, the ridge caps as a peak over the ridge either side of the cord, and the five paw pieces on the front gable centred 2.84" below the peak (dotted on page 1). Darken the inside of the door opening with a little Lamp Black.
  8. Hang: push a 10" floral wire through each floor hole, sit the house upright on a sturdy inner branch near the trunk and twist the wires round the branch; tie the gold loop to the branch above as a safety tie. About 40 min each once cut.

How we make it: materials, tools and steps

Paw-print hoop ornaments, 6" (DIY) · makes 10

Materials: Permanent fabric glue 118 ml (felt and glitter paws, scarf edges): 10 ml; Green floral wire 22 gauge, 3 x 118 yd: 2.2 yd; Glue sticks 7 mm, 96 pc: 20 sticks; White gesso 948 ml (primer; the white in the cream, biscuit and tan mixes): 17.5 ml; Metallic yarn, gold, 25 m (hanging loops): 2.5 m; Faylapa 6" bamboo embroidery hoops, 16-pk: 11 hoops; Aida fabric 14ct, white, 50 x 60 cm (19.7 x 23.6": four 9 x 9" pieces per sheet; tea-stained to the board's warm cream; ships in 48 h): 10 pc; Americana Dazzling Metallics Glorious Gold 60 ml: 35 ml; Black glitter cardstock 12 x 12", 10 sheets: 1.1 sheets; Felt sheet, black, 9 x 12" (backs for the paw ornaments: two 6" circles per sheet): 6 sheet; Dark red wired velvet ribbon 1.5" x 25 yd: 10.3 yd.

Tools: Craft brush set, 25 pc (doors, trim, details); Foam brush 1"; Mini hot glue gun (7 mm sticks); Erasable fabric marker, white (traces paws and circles on black felt); Wire cutter (every floral-wire cut: about 400); Extra-large moving box 24 x 20 x 20", flattened (the cutting surface under every knife cut); Scissors (office); Black tea bags, a kettle and a bowl (office kitchen).

Per ornament (template pages 3 and 9).

  1. Hoop: paint the outer ring only. Prime its outside face and front edge with gesso, then 2 coats of gold; leave the inner ring, the outer ring's inside face and the brass screw bare (paint there makes the clamp too tight and scuffs off). Paint one spare hoop with them. Cure 24 h.
  2. Face: cut the Aida into 9 x 9" pieces (4 per sheet, 2 spare). Tea-stain them: 4 black tea bags in 1 L of just-boiled water for 10 min, soak the pieces 10 min, rinse once and dry flat under a towel (no tea: 1/4 tsp deep ochre and a drop of burnt sienna in 1 cup of water). Stain an offcut strip first and let it dry to check: it should be the board's warm biscuit-cream, not white.
  3. Hoop it: lay a piece over the inner ring, press the outer ring down with the screw at the top, pull the edges evenly all round until drum-tight and tighten the screw. On the back trim the Aida to 1/2" outside the ring and hot-glue that margin to the inside of the inner ring.
  4. Paw: cut a 3.6" paw (pad + 4 toes, page 3) from the black glitter cardstock and glue it to the centre with fabric glue.
  5. Back: trace a 6" circle (page 9) on black felt with the white fabric marker, cut it out and hot-glue it to the back edge of the inner ring over the trimmed Aida, so the ornament is finished from behind.
  6. Bow and hanger: tie a 9" bow from 37" of the velvet (two 4.5" loops, 8" tails, V-notched), wire it just above the screw with 8" of floral wire, and tie a 25 cm gold cord loop through the screw to hang it; twist the wire ends round the branch.

How we make it: materials, tools and steps

Dog-bone ornaments, 9" (DIY) · makes 8

Materials: Green floral wire 22 gauge, 3 x 118 yd: 3.6 yd; Glue sticks 7 mm, 96 pc: 4 sticks; Student acrylic Burnt Sienna 250 ml (ships in 48 h): 8.9 ml; White gesso 948 ml (primer; the white in the cream, biscuit and tan mixes): 118.1 ml; Americana acrylic Deep Ochre 59 ml (tints gesso to cream, biscuit and tan): 9.8 ml; Metallic yarn, gold, 25 m (hanging loops): 4 m; White air-dry foam clay 500 g: 939 g; Mod Podge Matte 236 ml (sealer and sign glue): 73.8 ml.

Tools: Craft brush set, 25 pc (doors, trim, details); Foam brush 1"; Mini hot glue gun (7 mm sticks); Wire cutter (every floral-wire cut: about 400); Plastic drop sheet 8 x 12 ft (painting in the office); Aluminum foil (about 12 ft) (office); Toothpicks (16) (office); Two pencils (thickness guides) (office); Extra-large moving box 24 x 20 x 20", flattened (the cutting surface under every knife cut).

Per bone (template page 4: 9" long, knob span 4.8", shaft 2.4", about 1" thick). Start the day the clay lands: only the painting waits for the DeSerres parcel.

  1. Core: scrunch a 12 x 18" sheet of foil into a flat bone about 1/2" thick and 1/4" inside the page-4 outline all round, with a firm ball in each of the four knobs. Wire anchors: twist a small loop at one end of a 4" piece of floral wire and wrap its tail tightly round the foil inside each of the two upper knobs, with the loop just under the surface at the red marks.
  2. Clay: on a piece of the drop sheet, lay two pencils 5" apart as 1/4" thickness guides (or two of the 6 mm wood sticks once DeSerres arrives) and press about 120 g of foam clay between them into a 1/4" sheet with a flat flap cut from the XL moving box. Wrap the core, smooth the seams with a damp finger and shape four round knobs and a flat-faced shaft against the page-4 outline. Dry 48 h, turning once.
  3. Paint: 2 coats of the biscuit mix (1/2 cup gesso + 2 tsp deep ochre + 1 tsp burnt sienna); dry-brush burnt sienna on the edges and knobs; 1 coat of Mod Podge.
  4. Hang with two cords, level, like the board: drill a hole about 3/4" deep at each red mark by twisting a toothpick down to the wire anchor. Cut a 50 cm gold cord, knot each end twice, fill each hole with hot glue and push one knotted end into each, so the glue grips the anchor. The two cords rise from the upper knobs and the bone hangs level; hang it from the middle of the cord and wire the cord to the branch with 8" of floral wire.

How we make it: materials, tools and steps

Tartan ribbon cascades (DIY) · makes 5

Materials: Permanent fabric glue 118 ml (felt and glitter paws, scarf edges): 1.5 ml; Green floral wire 22 gauge, 3 x 118 yd: 9.2 yd; Tartan wired ribbon 4" x 10 yd: 16.4 yd.

Tools: Wire cutter (every floral-wire cut: about 400); Scissors (office).

  1. Cut five 118" lengths of the 4" tartan (rolls 1 and 2 of the cut plan under the big bows). V-notch one end of each and seal it with a thin bead of fabric glue.
  2. Space them evenly round the tree, about 72 degrees apart. Tuck the square end under the topper bow, about 8" below the tip, and wire it to the top stem with 6" of floral wire.
  3. Work down and slightly round the tree: let the ribbon lie over the branch tips for about 12", then pinch it up into a pouf about 3" proud (about 8" of ribbon) and wire the pinch to a branch with 6" of floral wire. Make 4 poufs per cascade, about 10 ties in all, and finish at the bottom branches about 12" off the floor with the notched tail hanging free.
  4. Wire 2-3 of the big tartan bows onto each cascade at a pouf, as on the board.

Big tartan bows, 11" (DIY) · makes 14

Materials: Permanent fabric glue 118 ml (felt and glitter paws, scarf edges): 7 ml; Green floral wire 22 gauge, 3 x 118 yd: 4.7 yd; Glue sticks 7 mm, 96 pc: 7 sticks; Tartan wired ribbon 4" x 10 yd: 25.2 yd.

Tools: Wire cutter (every floral-wire cut: about 400); Mini hot glue gun (7 mm sticks); Scissors (office).

Cut plan for the five 10-yd tartan rolls: roll 1 = three 118" cascades; roll 2 = two cascades, one 65" bow length and the 40" band for gift D; rolls 3-5 = five 65" bow lengths each (16 bows: 14 for the tree, 1 on top of gift D, 1 spare). Each bow: from a 65" (1.8 yd) length, cut a 6" knot piece. Leave a 15" tail, make one 5" loop to the left (about 11" of ribbon) and one to the right, pinch the centre with a 12" piece of floral wire, wrap the knot piece round the pinch and hot-glue it at the back, and leave a second 15" tail. V-notch both tails and run a thin bead of fabric glue along each notch. Twist the wire ends round a cascade pouf or a branch.

Velvet tree bows, 9" (DIY) · makes 5

Materials: Green floral wire 22 gauge, 3 x 118 yd: 1.7 yd; Dark red wired velvet ribbon 1.5" x 25 yd: 5.1 yd.

Tools: Wire cutter (every floral-wire cut: about 400); Scissors (office).

Each bow: 37" of the 1.5" velvet: two 4.5" loops and 8" tails with V-notches, pinched with a 12" floral wire (as the paw-ornament bows). Wire them between the tartan bows, mostly on the right side and lower half like the board.

How we make it: materials, tools and steps

Wrapped display gifts (DIY) · makes 4

Materials: Green floral wire 22 gauge, 3 x 118 yd: 0.8 yd; Glue sticks 7 mm, 96 pc: 3 sticks; Tartan wired ribbon 4" x 10 yd: 2.9 yd; Small moving box 18 x 11 x 12": 2 box; Medium moving box 16 x 16 x 16": 2 box; Red tartan wrapping paper 17" x 33 ft: 336 in; Natural burlap wired ribbon 1.5" x 20 yd: 16.2 yd; Box sealing tape, clear, 48 mm x 50 m: 12 m; Scotch Magic Tape 19 mm x 10 m, 3-pk (gift wrapping): 12 m; Kraft paw wrapping paper, 6 sheets 17 x 40": 2 sheets.

Tools: Art knife with 5 blades (foam board and cardboard); Steel and cork ruler 24"; Extra-large moving box 24 x 20 x 20", flattened (the cutting surface under every knife cut); Mini hot glue gun (7 mm sticks); Wire cutter (every floral-wire cut: about 400); Scissors (office); Pencil (office).

Boxes: A = small (18 x 11 x 12") as is, B = medium (16") as is, C = medium cut to 10" tall, D = small cut to 7" tall.

  1. Fold and packing-tape the top flaps of all four shut. For C and D, mark the new height up from the open bottom on each corner, rule a pencil line round the box and cut the walls down along it with the art knife against the ruler, on the cutting box. The open bottom sits on the floor, hidden.
  2. Tartan paper on A, B and C: cut two lengths of the box's girth (A 48", B 66", C 54") from the 17" roll and Magic-Tape them edge to edge on the back (1/2" overlap). Wrap so this join runs round the middle of the box, where the cream ribbon will cover it, with the girth overlap underneath; fold the ends like a parcel and tape (B's ends overlap only about 3/4": tape them well).
  3. Kraft paw paper on D: two 17 x 40" sheets taped side by side, wrapped the same way with the join under the tartan band.
  4. Ribbon: 1.5" cream burlap both ways round A, B and C, crossing on top over the paper join, ends taped underneath. On D, a 40" tartan band round the girth over the join and a 62" cream burlap band round the four sides, ends taped at the back.
  5. Bows: tie a 10" cream burlap bow (40": two 5" loops, 6" tails, V-notched, pinched with 6" of floral wire) for each box and hot-glue it at the ribbon crossing (on D, on the front of the cream band). Tie one big tartan bow (as the tree bows) and hot-glue it on top of D at the tartan band.

How we make it: materials, tools and steps

Natural wicker gift basket · bought, then finished by us

Materials: Green floral wire 22 gauge, 3 x 118 yd: 2 yd.

Tools: Wire cutter (every floral-wire cut: about 400).

Untie and remove the lace liner. Wire the jar (to the handle), the bone toy, the rope and the ball in with 12" floral wires through the wicker. Twist a 12" floral wire into a flat spiral card holder, push its stem into the wicker at the front and slip a gift card in so its face shows (the second card behind it), as on the board. Fold the throw paw-side out over the front edge and wire it at two corners.

Faux dog biscuits (DIY) · makes 64

Materials: Glue sticks 7 mm, 96 pc: 1 sticks; Student acrylic Burnt Sienna 250 ml (ships in 48 h): 5.1 ml; White gesso 948 ml (primer; the white in the cream, biscuit and tan mixes): 60.6 ml; Americana acrylic Deep Ochre 59 ml (tints gesso to cream, biscuit and tan): 10.1 ml; Dark red wired velvet ribbon 1.5" x 25 yd: 1.8 yd; White air-dry foam clay 500 g: 223.6 g; Mod Podge Matte 236 ml (sealer and sign glue): 37.9 ml; Kraft paw wrapping paper, 6 sheets 17 x 40": 3 sheets; Round wood sticks 6 mm x 15 cm, 30 pc (1/4" clay thickness guides, paint stirrers): 2 pc.

Tools: Craft brush set, 25 pc (doors, trim, details); Mini hot glue gun (7 mm sticks); Plastic drop sheet 8 x 12 ft (painting in the office); The 2.7" bone cutter (on the list); Toothpicks (3) (office); Round wood sticks 6 mm x 15 cm, 30 pc (1/4" clay thickness guides, paint stirrers); A foam-board offcut (on the list) to press the clay.

  1. Biscuits: on a piece of the drop sheet, press foam clay into a 1/4" sheet between two 6 mm wood sticks with a foam-board offcut, cut 64 bones with the 2.7" cutter (no cutter yet? trace the 3" outline on page 4 and cut with the knife), poke 3 dots in each with a toothpick and dry 24 h flat, turning once. Paint 2 coats of the tan mix (1/4 cup gesso + 2 tsp deep ochre + 1 tsp burnt sienna), then 1 coat of Mod Podge.
  2. Jar, ring by ring: stand 7 biscuits flat against the glass (long side level, face out), stuff crumpled kraft paw paper (3 spare sheets, brown side out) behind them until they press on the glass, and repeat for 7 rings up to the shoulder; pile the last 12 on top. Nudge them into place through the mouth with a wood stick.
  3. Wrap a 22" velvet band round the shoulder and hot-glue it at the back, tie a bow over the seam (44": two 5" loops, 9" tails), and fix the lid with 3 dots of hot glue (peels off later).

Cream fleece bone toy, 9" · bought, then finished by us

Materials: Black felt 8 x 12", 7 sheets: 0.1 sheets; Permanent fabric glue 118 ml (felt and glitter paws, scarf edges): 2 ml; Glue sticks 7 mm, 96 pc: 1 sticks.

Tools: Erasable fabric marker, white (traces paws and circles on black felt); Mini hot glue gun (7 mm sticks); Scissors (office).

Trace one 3" paw (template page 3) on the black felt with the white fabric marker and cut it out (pad + 4 toes). Part the sherpa pile, put a dot of hot glue under the pad and each toe and press 30 s, then run a thin bead of fabric glue round the edges; dry flat. Wire it into the basket with 12" of floral wire.

How we make it: materials, tools and steps

Golden retriever plush, sitting 12" · bought, then finished by us

Materials: Green floral wire 22 gauge, 3 x 118 yd: 7 yd.

Tools: Wire cutter (every floral-wire cut: about 400); Zip ties (supplied with the tree).

Each dog (about 100 g): fold a 72" floral wire in half, wrap the doubled wire round the belly under the scarf and twist both ends round a main branch near the trunk; add one of the organizers' zip ties round the body and branch, since the tree is moved several times. Sit it tilted back with the hind feet tucked onto the branch so the grey pads face down, and drape the scarf ends over the front paws. Under the tree, the dog and the cat sit side by side by the basket, wired to each other and to the basket handle with two 18" floral wires hidden under the scarves.

Grey tabby kitten plush, 9" (Aurora Miyoni) · bought, then finished by us

Materials: Green floral wire 22 gauge, 3 x 118 yd: 5 yd.

Tools: Wire cutter (every floral-wire cut: about 400); Scissors (office).

Each cat (about 136 g): snip off the gold Miyoni tag. Fold a 48" floral wire in half, wrap the doubled wire round the body behind the front legs, under the scarf, and twist both ends round a sturdy branch so the cat lies along it, face out. Under the tree it sits beside the dog (see the golden retriever).
